# Remit

> Least-privilege and lifecycle control for AI agent skills.

Remit audits the skills your coding agents already have, records static findings,
runs a behavioral canary when a container is available, pins installs by digest,
and blocks revoked digests at load time. Local-first, no account. Apache-2.0.

It is not a scanner score and not a marketplace. It is the evidence and lifecycle
layer under whatever registry or agent you already use. A finding is a rule match,
not proof of intent; a canary receipt is one observed run, not a guarantee.

## Facts

- 8 published `@remitlabs/*` packages at 0.1.1, Apache-2.0.
- 64 high-signal static rules.
- 73-specimen detection corpus: 64 attacks, 9 benign; static-only recall 64/64, benign flagged 0/9. Self-authored regression ceiling, not field accuracy.
- Measured on the founder's machine: 123 skills, 4 agent directories, 114 duplicate registrations.
- Eager context ~15,238 tokens vs ~150 with the MCP router (measured).
- Node.js 22.5+; Docker or Podman optional.
